digest.component_or_area: store write lock acquisition and retry
propositions: A store write that cannot acquire the write lock within its budget (60s × attempts) is permanently discarded with no retry mechanism, causing data loss even when the holder duration is the bottleneck rather than writer count.

The write-lock acquisition uses a single shared deadline for both fcntl and mkdir legs with non-blocking jitter-based polling, producing lottery-style fairness with no FIFO ordering, so fair queueing cannot prevent loss when a holder exceeds the entire budget.

Bounded retry-with-backoff inside acquire() converts terminal loss into latency by re-attempting acquisition (not write body replay) across up to 3 passes of 60s each plus ~1.5s backoff (~181.5s ceiling), safe because LockTimeout is raised before the caller's write body runs.

Five opt-in call sites (event_append.py ×3, txn.py ×1, push.py ×1) pass retries=_write_path_retries() reading REBAR_LOCK_RETRIES env var (default 2, clamped [0,10]), while all other callers keep retries=0 default for fail-fast behavior unchanged.

Writes that exhaust all retry passes raise LockTimeout naming cumulative wait plus holder details, with one warning logged per exhausted pass, while txn.py propagates the full exception message instead of a generic string.

No double-append occurs because the retry loop lives strictly inside acquire() and finishes before the caller's transaction body runs, verified by tests asserting exactly one event appended under contention.
